title: php2shell storyboard v3 (word-anchored, re-mapped onto docs/script/final_script.md)
wordsRef: Governments all over Europe just shut down a bunch of their own websites on purpose, because of this bug where hackers could take over a site without a password. It's in PHP, the language everyone loves, and about seven out of ten websites run on it. This bug was in there for like fourteen years before researchers using AI figured out how bad it was. They gave the PHP people a heads-up, but word got out before the fix was ready, and hackers were already trying to use it. Cloudflare says that once it was announced, they saw tens of thousands of hacking attempts in forty-five minutes, and millions within a day. But even with the fix out, somebody still has to install it on every single server. Plus something like half of PHP sites run versions so old they're not officially supported anymore. Even the FBI said if you can't update yet, just turn it off, which is basically tech support's answer to everything. And some of those governments did it before there was even a fix.
anchorRule: Every time is a word anchor {w, dt[, edge, gap, word]} (scripts/anchor/README.md): t = words[w].s + dt; edge 'e' = the word's END + dt; gap g = inside the pause after word w (its start + g x its length) + dt, so a cut stays in the pause on any take, or on the word boundary when the take has no pause there; 'word' is a text check. w is the 0-based index into wordsRef.split() (178 words). The film runs from {w:'START'} = 0 s to {w:'END'} = the timing's duration: the recorded lead-in (0.19 s before word 0) and tail (0.125 s after 'fix.') are NOT trimmed. Fixed-length moves (dives, exit trucks and tilts, the crane, landings) are anchored on their cut with a dt, so their duration never depends on the take. transitionIn.dur is 'auto' (resolve.py computes t1 - t0). Zoom is eased in log space (CineCamera channels); x / y are linear in the eased parameter; interp 'log-anchored' keeps an anchor point on its screen path.
timingFile: assets/timing_v3.json (the recorded take, 55.36 s; = assets/timing.json; resolve.py's default). assets/timing_est_v3.json (54.59 s, estimated: true) is kept as the planning estimate; the storyboard resolves cleanly against both.
timeline: v3 (word-anchored). No seconds anywhere except motion durations and the informational 'est' / 'rec' blocks (non-time keys 'sec' / 'len'). To get seconds: python3 -I scripts/anchor/resolve.py (default timing: assets/timing_v3.json). The v1/v2 storyboard (docs/storyboard.json) and scripts/timewarp.py no longer apply.
cameraRule: ONE owner per camera move: every move is a scene camera key below (ShotCam / CineCamera keys, or a World push with explicit to / at / dur). Film transitions add NO camera: every transitionIn is cut, matchcut or foreground-wipe (no push-through, no camera-continuous). Never rely on World's default push (+6 %) or its default pull-out after a push-through. Dive / exit segments are fixed-length and anchored on their cut; landings continue the dive's direction (log-zoom rates within ~1.5x across S04 -> S05; S01 -> S02 ~2.6x, accepted).

mascot.design: Our own small baby elephant (a nod to PHP's elePHPant, not the official mascot; built in src/lib/mascot): egg-shaped body, two big round ear flaps with salmon inners, a short curled trunk with 2-3 wrinkle ticks, a 3-strand head tuft, 3 downward-bowed back wrinkles (the cat's stripes), cream toenails, salmon soles, dot eyes, no tusks, no text, no logo. Loose 3.4 px ink with open contours (top of head between the ears and the base left open), flat fill offset 3 px right / 2 px down. Size: scale 1.0 (~96 px sitting) in the plaza vistas S01 / S12 (his gags must read there); scale 0.75 (~72 px, mascot.md's floor) in the PEAK vistas S08 (rest) and S09 Part B, so his tininess is a peak effect so his tininess is a peak effect; scale 1.2 (~115 px, reference 2's corgi size) in every medium and close scene so the small gags read on a phone; never below 0.75; in big camera moves he is kept at constant screen size (screen space). Plays the reference cat's role: perched, watching, reacting, one small physical gag per scene timed to its word (placed 0.25 s after the key word's focal event, near it), never covering the thing being explained, the sun or the counter. No look to camera in v3 (the 'right?' beat is gone with the two-steps setup). Crosses every transition (hop, fall, ride). Poses used, all from docs/mascot.md: sit-back, sit-front, stand-side, walk-side, trunk-up, hold, ears-cover, sleep, shrug. Props: NewLockIcon (S09, props lane); the S07 flyer is a scene overlay over the sit-front head bounds, not a prop; the S12 nod, the S09 sigh and the S03 proud puff are squash pulses. Supporting cast (not mascots): Bit, a solid-ink beetle (the bug: 16 px in wide shots, ~60 px in close-up) hiding in plain sight from frame 0 to the final frame; a sand-shelled snail (running gag S09, S11).
